title: Content Extraction: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Bytes To Trusted Text | BRIDGE. Tap each of the six things already taught in IR 102 (crawl frontier, politeness/robots.txt, traps and URL canonicalization, sitemaps and feeds, search APIs, seed selection and scope) to see what it guaranteed and what it never touched; then a two-state switch shows the same documentation page indexed as 2,070 words / ~3,000 tokens with 870 words of chrome versus 1,200 useful words after main-content extraction | Acquisition delivers bytes, not text: only 58% of what a naive innerText path indexes is the document, and the rest dilutes relevance and manufactures near-duplicates.

2. Boilerplate Or Content | Six DOM blocks (main article, nav tree, related links, footer, cookie banner, safety warning) with word counts, link density and site-wide repetition; a slider sets the link-density cutoff and a toggle adds the rule 'drop anything on >=90% of pages', recomputing words kept, chrome still indexed and needed blocks lost | Combining features works where any single rule fails: link density misses the prose-shaped cookie banner, and the template rule that catches it also deletes the site-wide safety warning, so removed regions must be kept as metadata and audited.

3. Which Structure Survives | Four preserve toggles (heading hierarchy, list boundaries, inline code marks, table headers) rewrite the extracted text of a worked HTML fragment live, collapsing to the fully flattened string when all are off; four downstream-use buttons (bag-of-words search, citation-grounded RAG, text-to-code retrieval, table question answering) declare which toggles they require and verdict the current representation | Preserve the minimum structure the declared downstream features need: flattening keeps every word and destroys which statements are list peers, that 100 is a literal, and that 1000 belongs to a named column.

4. Glyphs Without Order | Three sources in one panel: a two-column born-digital PDF whose reading order flips between naive sort-by-y interleaving and column clustering; a scanned page with an OCR confidence slider that corrupts O/0 and l/1 in an invoice line and routes accept / flag / retry at higher resolution / quarantine; and XLSX cell B2 (formula =A2*1.1, cached value 110, header 'Adjusted Price') with store-value / store-formula / store-both and which question each can answer | A non-empty, correctly spelled string can still be nonsense; store OCR confidence, engine, version and page references, and record both the value and the logic behind it.

5. Accept Or Discard | A quality record built from four sliders (pages parsed of 20, median words per page, replacement-character rate, OCR confidence) plus presets for the two worked documents, a fallbacks-untried/exhausted toggle and a web-research/compliance corpus toggle; it emits reason codes and routes to accept, retry with fallback, quarantine + alert, or discard | Routing has four outcomes and three are not discard: retry while a fallback is untried, quarantine when the corpus cannot afford a silent loss, and even a discard stores source ID, raw hash, reason codes and attempts — a lineage event, not an absence.
